records.literal_gloss: Open, Lebanon, your doors, and let devour fire your cedars.

en.L: Open your doors, Lebanon, \q and let fire devour your cedars.
en.B: Open your gates, Lebanon, \q so that fire may devour your cedars!
en.R: Lebanon, open your gates, \q and let fire burn up your cedar trees!

es.L: Abre tus puertas, oh Líbano, \q y que el fuego devore tus cedros.
es.B: ¡Abre tus puertas, Líbano, \q para que el fuego devore tus cedros!
es.R: ¡Líbano, abre tus puertas, \q y que el fuego queme tus cedros!

fr.L: Ouvre tes portes, Liban, \q et que le feu dévore tes cèdres.
fr.B: Ouvre tes portes, Liban, \q pour que le feu dévore tes cèdres !
fr.R: Liban, ouvre tes portes, \q et que le feu brûle tes cèdres !

sw.L: Fungua milango yako, ee Lebanoni, \q moto uile mierezi yako.
sw.B: Fungua malango yako, ee Lebanoni, \q ili moto uiteketeze mierezi yako!
sw.R: Ee Lebanoni, fungua malango yako, \q moto uiteketeze miti yako ya mierezi!

vi.L: Hỡi Li-ban, hãy mở các cửa của ngươi, \q để lửa thiêu nuốt những cây bá hương của ngươi.
vi.B: Hỡi Li-ban, hãy mở các cổng của ngươi, \q để lửa thiêu nuốt những cây bá hương của ngươi!
vi.R: Hỡi Li-ban, hãy mở cổng ra, \q để lửa thiêu rụi những cây bá hương của ngươi!

ko.L: 레바논아, 네 문들을 열어라. \q 불이 네 백향목들을 삼키게 하여라.
ko.B: 레바논아, 네 문들을 열어라. \q 불이 네 백향목들을 삼키게 하여라!
ko.R: 레바논아, 네 문들을 열어라. \q 불이 네 백향목들을 다 태워 버리게 하여라!

pt.L: Abre as tuas portas, Líbano, \q e que o fogo devore os teus cedros.
pt.B: Abre as tuas portas, Líbano, \q para que o fogo devore os teus cedros!
pt.R: Líbano, abre as tuas portas, \q e deixa o fogo queimar os teus cedros!

decisions.choice: a short poem of lament over the fall of the proud (verses 1-3)
decisions.reason: Verses 1-3 are a taunt in the form of a lament. The great trees of Lebanon and Bashan and the thickets of the Jordan are destroyed, and the shepherds wail. The poem links the promise of chapter 10, that the pride of the nations will be brought down (10:11), to the story of the shepherds that follows (11:4-17). It does not say which kingdom or which rulers it has in mind.

decisions.choice: Lebanon and its cedars: the proud and the powerful
decisions.reason: The cedars of Lebanon were the tallest and finest trees the Israelites knew, and they stand in the prophets for the pride of kings and nations (Isaiah 2:13; 10:33-34; Ezekiel 31:3-18). Jeremiah 22:6-7 uses them of the royal palace in Jerusalem. To "open your doors" to fire is to be left without defense.

decisions.choice: gates (B, R); cedar trees (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "doors" are the entrances to the land, its mountain passes; Balanced and Readable say "gates".

decisions.choice: "Líbano" addressed with tú
decisions.reason: Lebanon is spoken to as one, with tú, as the Hebrew is singular; the poem pictures the proud as great trees.

decisions.choice: tu (the prophet to Lebanon); as tuas portas (every level)
decisions.reason: Lebanon is spoken to as one, with "tu", as the prophets speak to a land or a city (m2). "Portas" serves at every level for the entrances to the land, where the English Balanced and Readable say "gates"; "portões" would suggest a garden gate.

source.text: הֵילֵ֤ל בְּרוֹשׁ֙ כִּֽי־נָ֣פַל אֶ֔רֶז אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַדִּרִ֖ים שֻׁדָּ֑דוּ הֵילִ֨ילוּ֙ אַלּוֹנֵ֣י בָשָׁ֔ן כִּ֥י יָרַ֖ד יַ֥עַר הַבָּצִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: Wail, juniper, for has fallen [the] cedar, for [the] majestic [ones] are destroyed; wail, oaks of Bashan, for has come down the inaccessible forest.

en.L: Wail, juniper, for the cedar has fallen, \q for the majestic [trees] are destroyed! \q Wail, oaks of Bashan, \q for the impenetrable forest has come down!
en.B: Wail, you junipers, for the cedar has fallen; \q the mighty trees are ruined! \q Wail, you oaks of Bashan, \q for the dense forest has been cut down!
en.R: Cry out in grief, you juniper trees, because the cedars have fallen. \q The great trees are destroyed. \q Cry out in grief, you oak trees of Bashan, \q because the thick forest has been cut down.

es.L: Gime, oh enebro, porque ha caído el cedro, \q porque los majestuosos [árboles] han sido destruidos. \q {{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, encinas de Basán, \q porque ha caído el bosque impenetrable.
es.B: ¡Gime, enebro, porque ha caído el cedro; \q los árboles poderosos han sido destruidos! \q ¡{{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, encinas de Basán, \q porque el bosque espeso ha sido talado!
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Lloren|Llorad}} de dolor, enebros, porque los cedros han caído! \q Los grandes árboles han sido destruidos. \q ¡{{plural_you:Lloren|Llorad}} de dolor, encinas de Basán, \q porque el bosque espeso ha sido talado!

fr.L: Hurle, genévrier, car le cèdre est tombé, \q car les majestueux sont dévastés ! \q Hurlez, chênes du Bashân, \q car la forêt impénétrable est abattue !
fr.B: Lamente-toi, genévrier, car le cèdre est tombé ; \q les arbres puissants sont ravagés ! \q Lamentez-vous, chênes du Bashân, \q car l’épaisse forêt est abattue !
fr.R: Pleurez de tristesse, genévriers, parce que les cèdres sont tombés. \q Les grands arbres sont détruits. \q Pleurez de tristesse, chênes du Bashân, \q parce que la forêt épaisse a été coupée.

sw.L: Piga yowe, ee mvinje, kwa maana mwerezi umeanguka, \q kwa maana [miti] ya fahari imeharibiwa! \q Pigeni yowe, enyi mialoni ya Bashani, \q kwa maana msitu usiopenyeka umeshuka!
sw.B: Pigeni yowe, enyi mivinje, kwa maana mwerezi umeanguka; \q miti mikubwa imeharibiwa! \q Pigeni yowe, enyi mialoni ya Bashani, \q kwa maana msitu mnene umekatwa!
sw.R: Lieni kwa huzuni, enyi miti ya mivinje, kwa sababu mierezi imeanguka. \q Miti mikubwa imeharibiwa. \q Lieni kwa huzuni, enyi mialoni ya Bashani, \q kwa sababu msitu mnene umekatwa.

vi.L: Hỡi cây bách xù, hãy than van, vì cây bá hương đã ngã, \q vì những [cây] oai nghi đã bị hủy phá! \q Hỡi các cây sồi Ba-san, hãy than van, \q vì rừng rậm không ai vào được đã bị đốn ngã!
vi.B: Hỡi những cây bách xù, hãy than van, vì cây bá hương đã ngã; \q những cây oai nghi đã bị tàn phá! \q Hỡi những cây sồi Ba-san, hãy than van, \q vì rừng rậm đã bị đốn hạ!
vi.R: Hỡi những cây bách xù, hãy khóc than, vì những cây bá hương đã ngã. \q Những cây lớn đã bị phá hủy. \q Hỡi những cây sồi ở Ba-san, hãy khóc than, \q vì khu rừng rậm đã bị đốn hạ.

ko.L: 향나무야, 울부짖어라. 백향목이 쓰러졌고, \q 위엄 있는 [나무들이] 망하였다! \q 바산의 상수리나무들아, 울부짖어라. \q 빽빽한 숲이 무너졌다!
ko.B: 향나무들아, 울부짖어라. 백향목이 쓰러졌다. \q 장엄한 나무들이 망하였다! \q 바산의 상수리나무들아, 울부짖어라. \q 울창한 숲이 베어져 넘어졌다!
ko.R: 향나무들아, 슬피 울어라. 백향목들이 쓰러졌다. \q 큰 나무들이 망가졌다. \q 바산의 상수리나무들아, 슬피 울어라. \q 울창한 숲이 베어져 넘어졌다.

pt.L: Uiva, zimbro, porque o cedro caiu, \q porque as [árvores] majestosas foram destruídas! \q Uivem, carvalhos de Basã, \q porque o bosque impenetrável caiu!
pt.B: Uivem, zimbros, porque o cedro caiu; \q as árvores imponentes foram arruinadas! \q Uivem, carvalhos de Basã, \q porque a floresta densa foi derrubada!
pt.R: Chorem de tristeza, zimbros, porque os cedros caíram. \q As grandes árvores foram destruídas. \q Chorem de tristeza, carvalhos de Basã, \q porque a floresta fechada foi derrubada.

decisions.choice: junipers, the oaks of Bashan: the other great trees of the land
decisions.reason: The tree named first is a tall evergreen, a juniper or cypress, used with cedar for the finest buildings (1 Kings 5:22). Bashan, east of the Sea of Galilee, was famous for its oaks (Isaiah 2:13; Ezekiel 27:6). If even the cedar has fallen, the lesser trees have reason to wail.

decisions.choice: the impenetrable forest: following the reading tradition
alternatives: the forest of the vintage (the written form)
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew can be read "the forest of the vintage", that is, the grape harvest. The reading tradition gives "the inaccessible forest", a forest too thick to enter, which fits the picture and is followed here.

decisions.choice: Wail (L, B); Cry out in grief (R); juniper
decisions.reason: "Wail" is "Cry out in grief" at Readable, as in Isaiah, and the tree is a juniper, as in Isaiah 14:8.

decisions.choice: "Gime" / "Giman" (L, B); "Lloren de dolor" (R); "enebro", "encinas de Basán"
decisions.reason: The call to wail follows the Spanish prophets (Isaiah 13:6); the trees keep their published names (2 Kings 19:23; Isaiah 2:13). The plural trees are addressed directly, so the plural verbs take plural_you; the single juniper of L and B takes tú.

decisions.choice: "Hurle" (L), "Lamente-toi" (B), "Pleurez de tristesse" (R); singular and plural as the Hebrew
decisions.reason: The juniper is addressed in the singular and the oaks in the plural in Hebrew; L and B keep the switch, Readable makes both plural as the English.

decisions.choice: "cây bách xù" for the juniper (berosh)
decisions.reason: The tree is uncertain (juniper, cypress or fir); "bách xù" follows the English, a reviewer may prefer the published word for berosh elsewhere.

decisions.choice: "Piga yowe" / "Pigeni yowe" (L, B); "Lieni kwa huzuni" (R); "mvinje" for the juniper
decisions.reason: "Kupiga yowe" is the loud wail of mourning; the trees are addressed as mourners. "Mvinje" is the Swahili name for the casuarina and similar conifers, the nearest common tree name for the juniper or cypress.

decisions.choice: "울부짖어라" (L, B); "슬피 울어라" (R); "향나무"
decisions.reason: Modern 해라체 imperatives (term sheet); the juniper is "향나무" as in the Korean Isaiah 14:8.

decisions.choice: Uiva/Uivem (L, B); Chorem de tristeza (R); zimbro; os carvalhos de Basã
decisions.reason: The cry is "uivar" at Literal and Balanced, the verb Jeremiah 25:34 uses in Portuguese for the shepherds' wail, and Readable says "chorem de tristeza", as the English Readable does (r-en-1). The tree is "zimbro", as Isaiah 14:8 has it in Portuguese; "Basã" is the usual form of Bashan.

source.text: ק֚וֹל יִֽלְלַ֣ת הָרֹעִ֔ים כִּ֥י שֻׁדְּדָ֖ה אַדַּרְתָּ֑ם ק֚וֹל שַׁאֲגַ֣ת כְּפִירִ֔ים כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד גְּא֥וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] sound of [the] wailing of the shepherds, for is destroyed their glory; [the] sound of [the] roaring of young lions, for is destroyed [the] pride of the Jordan.

en.L: [Listen to] the sound of the shepherds' wailing, \q for their glory is destroyed; \q the sound of the young lions' roaring, \q for the pride of the Jordan is destroyed.
en.B: Hear the shepherds wail, \q for their splendor is ruined! \q Hear the young lions roar, \q for the Jordan's thickets are laid waste!
en.R: Listen to the shepherds crying out in grief, \q because their rich pastures are ruined. \q Listen to the young lions roaring, \q because the thick bushes along the Jordan River are destroyed.

es.L: [{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}] la voz del gemido de los pastores, \q porque su gloria ha sido destruida; \q la voz del rugido de los leoncillos, \q porque la espesura del Jordán ha sido destruida.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}} cómo gimen los pastores, \q porque su esplendor ha sido arruinado! \q ¡{{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}} cómo rugen los leones jóvenes, \q porque la espesura del Jordán ha sido asolada!
es.R: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} a los pastores que lloran de dolor, \q porque sus ricos pastos han sido arruinados. \q {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} a los leones jóvenes que rugen, \q porque los matorrales espesos a lo largo del río Jordán han sido destruidos.

fr.L: [Écoutez] la voix de la lamentation des bergers, \q car leur gloire est dévastée ; \q la voix du rugissement des lionceaux, \q car l’orgueil du Jourdain est dévasté.
fr.B: Écoutez les bergers qui gémissent, \q car leur splendeur est ruinée ! \q Écoutez les jeunes lions qui rugissent, \q car les fourrés du Jourdain sont ravagés !
fr.R: Écoutez les bergers qui pleurent de tristesse, \q parce que leurs riches pâturages sont détruits. \q Écoutez les jeunes lions qui rugissent, \q parce que les buissons épais au bord du Jourdain sont détruits.

sw.L: [Sikia] sauti ya kuomboleza kwa wachungaji, \q kwa maana utukufu wao umeharibiwa; \q sauti ya kunguruma kwa wana-simba, \q kwa maana kiburi cha Yordani kimeharibiwa.
sw.B: Sikia wachungaji wakiomboleza, \q kwa maana fahari yao imeharibiwa! \q Sikia wana-simba wakinguruma, \q kwa maana vichaka vya Yordani vimeharibiwa!
sw.R: Sikilizeni wachungaji wakilia kwa huzuni, \q kwa sababu malisho yao mazuri yameharibiwa. \q Sikilizeni wana-simba wakinguruma, \q kwa sababu vichaka vinene kando ya mto Yordani vimeharibiwa.

vi.L: [Hãy nghe] tiếng than van của những người chăn, \q vì vinh quang của họ đã bị hủy phá; \q tiếng gầm thét của những sư tử tơ, \q vì niềm kiêu hãnh của Giô-đanh đã bị hủy phá.
vi.B: Hãy nghe tiếng những người chăn than van, \q vì cảnh huy hoàng của họ đã tiêu tan! \q Hãy nghe tiếng những sư tử tơ gầm thét, \q vì những bụi rậm của sông Giô-đanh đã bị tàn phá!
vi.R: Hãy nghe những người chăn khóc than, \q vì những đồng cỏ tốt tươi của họ đã bị tàn phá. \q Hãy nghe những sư tử tơ gầm thét, \q vì những bụi cây rậm rạp dọc sông Giô-đanh đã bị phá hủy.

ko.L: 목자들의 울부짖는 소리[를 들어라]. \q 그들의 영광이 망하였기 때문이다. \q 젊은 사자들의 으르렁거리는 소리[를 들어라]. \q 요단의 자랑이 망하였기 때문이다.
ko.B: 목자들이 울부짖는 소리를 들어라. \q 그들의 화려한 목장이 망하였다! \q 젊은 사자들이 으르렁거리는 소리를 들어라. \q 요단 강가의 우거진 숲이 황폐해졌다!
ko.R: 목자들이 슬피 우는 소리를 들어라. \q 그들의 기름진 목장이 망가졌기 때문이다. \q 젊은 사자들이 으르렁거리는 소리를 들어라. \q 요단 강가의 우거진 덤불이 망가졌기 때문이다.

pt.L: [Ouçam] o som do uivo dos pastores, \q porque a sua glória foi destruída; \q o som do rugido dos leõezinhos, \q porque o orgulho do Jordão foi destruído.
pt.B: Ouçam os pastores uivando, \q porque o seu esplendor foi arruinado! \q Ouçam os leões novos rugindo, \q porque as matas do Jordão foram devastadas!
pt.R: Escutem os pastores chorando de tristeza, \q porque os seus pastos ricos foram arruinados. \q Escutem os leões novos rugindo, \q porque o mato fechado nas margens do rio Jordão foi destruído.

decisions.choice: the wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is destroyed: the rulers lament their loss
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 25:34-36 hears the same cry: "Wail, you shepherds ... for the LORD is destroying their pasture." The shepherds stand for the rulers (10:3). Their "glory" is the richness of their pastures, the source of their wealth; the same word is used of a fine cloak in 13:4.

decisions.choice: the young lions; the pride of the Jordan: the thick growth along the river where lions lived
decisions.reason: The Jordan valley was lined with dense thickets where lions made their dens (Jeremiah 12:5; 49:19). When the thickets are destroyed, the lions roar for the loss of their home. The lions, like the shepherds, may stand for rulers (Ezekiel 19:1-9).

decisions.choice: [Listen to] (L); Listen to (B, R); the thickets of the Jordan (B); the thick bushes along the Jordan River (R); their rich pastures (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins each half with "the sound of", a cry calling for attention (Isaiah 40:3); Literal brackets "Listen to", and Balanced ("Hear") and Readable ("Listen to") give it as a command. Balanced and Readable say what "the pride of the Jordan" was, and Readable what the shepherds' glory was (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: "la espesura del Jordán" (L, B); "los matorrales espesos a lo largo del río Jordán" (R)
decisions.reason: The pride of the Jordan is its thick growth, worded as in Jeremiah 12:5 and 49:19 in Spanish.

decisions.choice: "소리가 [들린다]" (L)
decisions.reason: Korean cannot leave "the sound of" without a verb; Literal supplies the plainest one, and Balanced and Readable say "들어라", "들어 보아라" as the English does.

source.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑י רְעֵ֖ה אֶת־צֹ֥אן הַהֲרֵגָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh my God: Shepherd the flock of the slaughter,

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God: "Shepherd the flock [doomed] for slaughter,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} my God says this: "Shepherd the flock that is marked for slaughter,

es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mi Dios dice esto: «Apacienta el rebaño destinado a la matanza,

vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của tôi phán như vầy: "Con hãy chăn bầy chiên đã bị định cho lò sát sinh,
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của tôi phán: "Con hãy chăm sóc những con chiên sắp bị đem đi giết thịt.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD my God: the prophet tells, in prose, of a part he was told to act
decisions.reason: From here to verse 16 the prophet tells in the first person how the LORD told him to act the part of a shepherd, and what happened. Like Hosea's marriage (Hosea 1-3) or Jeremiah's loincloth (Jeremiah 13:1-11), the actions are a message. The passage is among the hardest in the prophets: the flock, its buyers and sellers, the three shepherds and the staffs are not explained, and readers have identified them in very different ways. The translation keeps to what the text says.

decisions.choice: the flock for slaughter: a flock raised only to be killed
decisions.reason: Sheep raised for slaughter were bought and sold for their meat; no one cared for them for their own sake. The people are like such a flock, exploited by those who should protect them (Psalm 44:23; Jeremiah 12:3). Verse 5 says who these exploiters are.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD my God (L); The LORD my God says this (B); This is what the LORD my God says (R); quotation marks
decisions.reason: The formula follows the wording set in Isaiah, with "my God" added as in the Hebrew. In this prose story the LORD's words are quoted with quotation marks, as in Jeremiah 13:1. Literal and Balanced end with a comma, because the sentence goes on into verse 5; Literal brackets "doomed".

decisions.choice: God's words to Zechariah in this acted sign take quotation marks, as the English does, and God says "con" (B, R) to him
alternatives: no quotation marks, as in the oracles
decisions.reason: The prophet tells in prose what he was told to do; the English quotes it, and Vietnamese follows. "Con" at B and R is the term sheet's address from God to the prophet.

decisions.choice: "잡혀 죽을 양 떼" (L, B); "곧 잡혀 죽을 양들" (R)
decisions.reason: The flock is raised only to be killed (meaning decision); the prophet tells this in prose, so God's words to him take quotation marks as in the English.

decisions.choice: The prophet's account of the two shepherds (11:4-17): God's words are quoted with « » as narrative dialogue, as the English; what the prophet did is in the passé simple at L and B and the passé composé at R
decisions.reason: A first-person story told in prose, which the term sheet treats as narrative.

decisions.choice: "troupeau" and "faire paître" (L, B), "moutons" and "prendre soin" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet's shepherd words; "faire paître" is the French verb for a shepherd's work.

decisions.choice: "Apacienta" (L, B); "Cuida de las ovejas" (R); quotation marks
decisions.reason: The prophet tells in prose of the part he was told to act, so God's words to him take « », as the English has quotation marks.

decisions.choice: quotation marks for the LORD's instructions in 11:4-6, 13 and 15-16
decisions.reason: This passage is a prose narrative of a part the prophet is told to act, so, as the English does, Swahili quotes the LORD's words with quotation marks; the oracles elsewhere take none.

decisions.choice: Apascenta (L, B); Cuida (R); tu (God to the prophet)
decisions.reason: God speaks to the prophet with "tu" through the story (verses 4-6, 13, 15-16). "Apascentar" is the Portuguese verb for a shepherd leading his flock to pasture (m2); Readable says "cuidar", as the English Readable says "take care of".

ko.R: 양들을 사는 사람들은 양들을 잡아도 벌을 받지 않는다. 양들을 파는 사람들은 '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 찬양하여라! 이제 나는 부자가 되었다!' 하고 말한다. 양들의 목자들조차 양들을 불쌍히 여기지 않는다.

decisions.choice: buyers, sellers and shepherds: those who profit from the flock
decisions.reason: The buyers kill the sheep for meat, the sellers grow rich from the sale, and the shepherds who should care for them do nothing. The picture is of rulers, foreign and native, who used the people for their own gain (Ezekiel 34:2-6). The text does not say who they were.

decisions.choice: are not held guilty: they suffer no punishment and feel no guilt
decisions.reason: The verb means to be guilty or to bear the penalty for guilt. The buyers act as though harming this flock carried no blame (Jeremiah 2:3; 50:7).

decisions.choice: Blessed be the LORD, for I have become rich: greed in the language of piety
decisions.reason: The seller thanks God for his profit, made from the flock's destruction. Hosea 12:9 hears the same boast from a cheating merchant. The words are a bitter irony.

decisions.choice: go unpunished (B); are not punished (R); Praise the LORD (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "Praise the LORD" for the blessing formula, as English speakers thank God. The words of the sellers are quoted within the LORD's words, so they take single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "Bendito [sea]" (L); "Alabado sea" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The seller's pious words are kept at L; B and R use the common Spanish praise formula, as the English uses "Praise the LORD". The inner quotation takes “ ”.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 찬양하여라"
decisions.reason: "Blessed be the LORD" said by the greedy seller (meaning decision); the particle "를" reads after both forms of the span.

vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không còn thương xót dân cư trong xứ nữa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy. Ta sắp phó mọi người vào tay người lân cận mình và vào tay vua mình. Chúng sẽ chà đạp xứ, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không giải cứu ai khỏi quyền lực của chúng."
vi.R: Ta sẽ không còn thương xót những người sống trong xứ nữa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Ta sẽ để dân chúng rơi vào quyền lực của những người lân cận và của vua họ. Chúng sẽ tàn phá xứ, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không giải cứu ai khỏi tay chúng."

ko.L: 내가 다시는 이 땅의 주민들을 불쌍히 여기지 않을 것이기 때문이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. 보라, 내가 사람들을 각자 자기 이웃의 손과 자기 왕의 손에 넘겨주겠다. 그들이 이 땅을 짓밟아도, 내가 [이 땅을] 그들의 손에서 건져 내지 않겠다."
ko.B: 이제 나는 이 땅에 사는 사람들을 더 이상 불쌍히 여기지 않겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내가 사람들을 저마다 이웃의 손과 왕의 손에 넘겨주겠다. 그들이 이 땅을 짓밟아도, 내가 그들의 손에서 아무도 건져 내지 않겠다."
ko.R: 나는 이 땅에 사는 사람들을 더 이상 불쌍히 여기지 않겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 나는 사람들이 이웃과 왕의 손에 넘어가게 하겠다. 그들이 이 땅을 망가뜨려도, 나는 아무도 그들에게서 구해 주지 않겠다."

pt.L: Porque não terei mais compaixão dos habitantes da terra, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. E eis que entrego toda a humanidade, cada um na mão do seu próximo e na mão do seu rei; e eles esmagarão a terra, e não [a] livrarei da mão deles."
pt.B: Porque não terei mais pena dos que moram na terra, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Vou entregar cada um nas mãos do seu próximo e nas mãos do seu rei. Eles esmagarão a terra, e não livrarei ninguém do poder deles."
pt.R: Não vou mais sentir pena das pessoas que moram na terra, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Vou deixar o povo cair no poder dos seus vizinhos e do seu rei. Eles vão destruir a terra, e eu não vou livrar ninguém das mãos deles."

decisions.choice: I will no longer have compassion: the LORD hands the people over to judgment
decisions.reason: The LORD answers the shepherds' lack of compassion (verse 5) with the same verb: he too will no longer spare the people. The "inhabitants of the land" are most likely the people of Israel. The LORD gives them over to their own neighbors and rulers, and does not rescue them, a judgment like the one Jeremiah spoke (Jeremiah 13:14; 21:7).

decisions.choice: each into the hand of their neighbor and their king: civil strife and harsh rule
decisions.reason: The people will turn on one another, and their king will oppress them. "His king" may be the people's own ruler or a foreign one. To be "in the hand" of someone is to be in their power.

decisions.choice: each into the hand of their neighbor (L, B); their (gender setting)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "each ... his" means everyone, men and women, so Literal and Balanced take the gender setting. Readable speaks of "the people" in the plural and needs no setting. "Declares the LORD" follows the wording set in Isaiah, and the LORD's words, quoted since verse 4, end here.

decisions.choice: "cada uno en mano de su prójimo"
decisions.reason: Spanish "cada uno" and "su" cover both readings of the English gender setting, so no span is needed.

decisions.choice: {{gender:les humains|les hommes}} (L) on the noun; "chacun ... son prochain ... son roi" with no span
decisions.reason: French puts the setting on the noun for ha-adam; "chacun" and "son" are already inclusive where the English needs {{gender:their|his}}.

decisions.choice: "kila mtu ... jirani yake", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Mtu" and "-ake" already cover both sexes, so Swahili needs no gender span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: "mình" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "mình" refers back to anyone, man or woman, so there is only one wording.

decisions.choice: "각각 그 이웃", "각자의 이웃", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean uses no pronoun here, and "사람", "각자" already include men and women.

decisions.choice: cada um na mão do seu próximo e na mão do seu rei; no gender span
decisions.reason: The English puts "his neighbor ... his king" under the gender setting at Literal and Balanced (r-en-1). Portuguese "cada um ... do seu" is already the inclusive generic form (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7), so there is no span.

source.text: וָֽאֶרְעֶה֙ אֶת־צֹ֣אן הַֽהֲרֵגָ֔ה לָכֵ֖ן עֲנִיֵּ֣י הַצֹּ֑אן וָאֶקַּֽח־לִ֞י שְׁנֵ֣י מַקְל֗וֹת לְאַחַ֞ד קָרָ֤אתִי נֹ֨עַם֙ וּלְאַחַד֙ קָרָ֣אתִי חֹֽבְלִ֔ים וָאֶרְעֶ֖ה אֶת־הַצֹּֽאן׃

records.literal_gloss: And I shepherded the flock of the slaughter, therefore the afflicted of the flock. And I took for myself two staffs; one I called Favor, and one I called Union; and I shepherded the flock.

en.L: So I shepherded the flock [doomed] for slaughter, truly the afflicted of the flock. And I took for myself two staffs: one I called Favor, and one I called Union; and I shepherded the flock.
en.B: So I became shepherd of the flock marked for slaughter, the most afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs; one I named Favor and the other Union, and I shepherded the flock.
en.R: So I took care of the sheep that were going to be slaughtered, the sheep that were suffering most. I took two shepherd's staffs. I named one of them Favor and the other Union. Then I took care of the sheep.

es.L: Así que apacenté el rebaño [destinado] a la matanza, en verdad los afligidos del rebaño. Y tomé para mí dos cayados: a uno lo llamé Favor y al otro lo llamé Unión; y apacenté el rebaño.
es.B: Así que me hice pastor del rebaño destinado a la matanza, los más afligidos del rebaño. Tomé dos cayados; a uno le puse por nombre Favor y al otro Unión, y apacenté el rebaño.
es.R: Así que cuidé de las ovejas que iban a ser sacrificadas, las ovejas que más sufrían. Tomé dos cayados de pastor. A uno le puse por nombre Favor, y al otro, Unión. Entonces cuidé de las ovejas.

fr.L: Alors je fis paître le troupeau [destiné] à l’abattage, vraiment les malheureux du troupeau. Et je pris pour moi deux bâtons : l’un, je l’appelai Faveur, et l’autre, je l’appelai Union ; et je fis paître le troupeau.
fr.B: Je devins donc le berger du troupeau promis à l’abattoir, les plus malheureux du troupeau. Je pris deux bâtons ; je nommai l’un Faveur et l’autre Union, et je fis paître le troupeau.
fr.R: Alors je me suis occupé des moutons qui allaient être abattus, les moutons qui souffraient le plus. J’ai pris deux bâtons de berger. J’ai appelé l’un Faveur et l’autre Union. Puis je me suis occupé des moutons.

sw.L: Basi nikalichunga kundi [lililowekwa] kwa ajili ya kuchinjwa, kweli wanyonge wa kundi. Nami nikajitwalia fimbo mbili: moja nikaiita Fadhili, na nyingine nikaiita Umoja; nikalichunga kundi.
sw.B: Basi nikawa mchungaji wa kundi lililotengwa kwa ajili ya kuchinjwa, wale walioteseka kuliko wote katika kundi. Nikachukua fimbo mbili; moja nikaiita Fadhili na nyingine Umoja, nikalichunga kundi.
sw.R: Basi nikawatunza kondoo ambao wangechinjwa, kondoo walioteseka kuliko wengine wote. Nikachukua fimbo mbili za mchungaji. Moja nikaiita Fadhili na nyingine Umoja. Kisha nikawatunza kondoo.

vi.L: Vậy tôi chăn bầy chiên [đã định] cho sự giết mổ, thật là những con khốn khổ nhất trong bầy. Tôi lấy cho mình hai cây gậy: một cây tôi gọi là Ân Huệ, và một cây tôi gọi là Hiệp Nhất; rồi tôi chăn bầy chiên.
vi.B: Vậy tôi làm người chăn bầy chiên đã bị định cho lò sát sinh, là những con khốn khổ nhất trong bầy. Tôi lấy hai cây gậy; một cây tôi đặt tên là Ân Huệ, cây kia là Hiệp Nhất, và tôi chăn bầy chiên.
vi.R: Vậy tôi chăm sóc những con chiên sắp bị đem đi giết thịt, là những con khốn khổ nhất. Tôi lấy hai cây gậy chăn chiên. Tôi đặt tên một cây là Ân Huệ và cây kia là Hiệp Nhất. Rồi tôi chăm sóc đàn chiên.

ko.L: 그래서 내가 잡혀 죽을 양 떼, 곧 양 떼 가운데 고난받는 것들을 쳤다. 내가 나를 위하여 지팡이 두 개를 가져다가, 하나는 '은총'이라 부르고 하나는 '연합'이라 불렀다. 그리고 내가 양 떼를 쳤다.
ko.B: 그래서 나는 잡혀 죽을 운명에 놓인 양 떼, 그 가운데서도 가장 고난받는 양들의 목자가 되었다. 나는 지팡이 두 개를 가져다가, 하나는 '은총'이라 하고 다른 하나는 '연합'이라 하고, 양 떼를 돌보았다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 곧 잡혀 죽을 양들, 가장 고통받는 양들을 돌보았다. 나는 목자의 지팡이 두 개를 가져다가, 하나는 '은총'이라고 이름 짓고 다른 하나는 '연합'이라고 이름 지었다. 그리고 양들을 돌보았다.

pt.L: Então apascentei o rebanho [destinado] à matança, verdadeiramente os aflitos do rebanho. E tomei para mim duas varas: a uma chamei Favor, e à outra chamei União; e apascentei o rebanho.
pt.B: Então me tornei pastor do rebanho marcado para a matança, as ovelhas mais aflitas do rebanho. Peguei duas varas; a uma dei o nome de Favor, e à outra, União; e apascentei o rebanho.
pt.R: Então cuidei das ovelhas que iam ser abatidas, as ovelhas que mais sofriam. Peguei dois cajados de pastor. A um dei o nome de Favor, e ao outro, União. E cuidei das ovelhas.

decisions.choice: truly the afflicted of the flock: following the Hebrew text
alternatives: for the sheep traders (following the Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "therefore (or "truly") the afflicted of the flock". The Septuagint read the same letters as one word, "for the Canaanites", that is, the traders, giving "the flock doomed to slaughter for the sheep traders". The same choice comes again in verse 11. Many modern translations follow the Greek. The Hebrew text is kept here; it speaks of the poor of the flock, whom the shepherd cares for.

decisions.choice: Favor and Union: the names of the two staffs
decisions.reason: A shepherd carried a staff to guide and guard the flock (Psalm 23:4). The first name means pleasantness, grace or favor: the LORD's kindness that protects the flock (Psalm 90:17 uses the word). The second means "bonds" or "cords", the ties that bind the people together. Verses 10 and 14 explain the names when the staffs are broken.

decisions.choice: Favor, Union (every level)
decisions.reason: The names are translated at every level, because the story turns on what they mean (m2). Readable says "shepherd's staffs".

decisions.choice: "Favor", "Unión"
decisions.reason: The names of the two staffs are translated and capitalized at every level, as in the English; "cayado" is the shepherd's staff.

decisions.choice: "Faveur" and "Union" for the two staffs, at every level
decisions.reason: Names that say plainly what each staff stands for (God's favour, the bond between Judah and Israel), as the English.

decisions.choice: "Fadhili" (Favor) and "Umoja" (Union), capitalized as names, at every level
decisions.reason: "Neema" is kept for grace in the New Testament; "fadhili" is God's goodwill and kindness, the sense of Hebrew no'am here. "Umoja" says the bond the second staff stands for (11:14).

decisions.choice: the staffs' names "Ân Huệ" (Favor) and "Hiệp Nhất" (Union), capitalised at every level
decisions.reason: Vietnamese names keep their meaning in plain words, so the sign is clear; "Hiệp Nhất" points to the bond between Judah and Israel broken in verse 14.

decisions.choice: '은총' and '연합' as the staffs' names, in inner quotation marks
decisions.reason: The English capitalizes Favor and Union as names; Korean marks them with single quotation marks. "은총" keeps the sense of favor and grace; "연합" the binding together of verse 14.

decisions.choice: Favor; União (every level); varas (L, B), cajados de pastor (R)
decisions.reason: The names of the staffs are translated at every level, as the English does (r-en-1), since the story turns on them (m2): "Favor" for the LORD's kindness and "União" for the bonds that hold the people together, each with a capital as a name.

source.text: וָאַכְחִ֛ד אֶת־שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הָרֹעִ֖ים בְּיֶ֣רַח אֶחָ֑ד וַתִּקְצַ֤ר נַפְשִׁי֙ בָּהֶ֔ם וְגַם־נַפְשָׁ֖ם בָּחֲלָ֥ה בִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I destroyed the three shepherds in one month; and my soul was short with them, and also their soul loathed me.

en.L: And I wiped out the three shepherds in one month. And my soul was impatient with them, and their soul also loathed me.
en.B: In one month I got rid of the three shepherds. Then I lost patience with the flock, and they, for their part, loathed me.
en.R: In one month I got rid of the three shepherds. Then I grew tired of the sheep, and they hated me.

es.L: Y eliminé a los tres pastores en un mes. Y mi alma se impacientó con ellos, y también su alma me aborreció.
es.B: En un mes me deshice de los tres pastores. Luego perdí la paciencia con el rebaño, y ellos, por su parte, me aborrecieron.
es.R: En un mes me deshice de los tres pastores. Luego me cansé de las ovejas, y ellas me odiaron.

fr.L: Et je fis disparaître les trois bergers en un seul mois. Et mon âme perdit patience avec eux, et leur âme aussi me prit en dégoût.
fr.B: En un seul mois, je me débarrassai des trois bergers. Puis je perdis patience avec le troupeau, et lui, de son côté, me prit en dégoût.
fr.R: En un seul mois, je me suis débarrassé des trois bergers. Ensuite, j’en ai eu assez des moutons, et eux m’ont détesté.

sw.L: Nami nikawakatilia mbali wale wachungaji watatu katika mwezi mmoja. Na nafsi yangu ikakosa subira juu yao, nayo nafsi yao pia ikanichukia.
sw.B: Katika mwezi mmoja niliwaondoa wale wachungaji watatu. Kisha nikachoshwa na kundi, nao pia wakanichukia.
sw.R: Katika mwezi mmoja niliwaondoa wale wachungaji watatu. Kisha nikachoshwa na kondoo, nao wakanichukia.

vi.L: Tôi đã diệt trừ ba người chăn trong một tháng. Linh hồn tôi đã mất kiên nhẫn với chúng, và linh hồn chúng cũng ghê tởm tôi.
vi.B: Trong một tháng tôi đã loại bỏ ba người chăn. Rồi tôi hết kiên nhẫn với bầy chiên, và chúng cũng ghê tởm tôi.
vi.R: Trong một tháng tôi đã loại bỏ ba người chăn. Rồi tôi chán ngán đàn chiên, và chúng cũng ghét tôi.

ko.L: 내가 한 달 안에 세 목자를 없애 버렸다. 내 영혼은 그것들에게 참지 못하였고, 그것들의 영혼도 나를 싫어하였다.
ko.B: 나는 한 달 안에 목자 셋을 없애 버렸다. 그 뒤 나는 양 떼를 더 이상 참을 수 없었고, 양 떼도 나를 싫어하였다.
ko.R: 나는 한 달 만에 목자 셋을 없애 버렸다. 그 뒤 나는 양들에게 지쳐 버렸고, 양들도 나를 미워했다.

pt.L: E eliminei os três pastores num só mês. E a minha alma perdeu a paciência com elas, e também a alma delas me detestou.
pt.B: Num só mês, eu me livrei dos três pastores. Depois perdi a paciência com o rebanho, e ele, por sua vez, me detestou.
pt.R: Num só mês, eu me livrei dos três pastores. Depois me cansei das ovelhas, e elas me odiaram.

decisions.choice: the three shepherds in one month: rulers removed quickly, who they were is unknown
decisions.reason: The text does not say who the three shepherds were. Readers have suggested kings of Israel who reigned briefly (2 Kings 15:8-15), high priests, foreign rulers, or the three offices of king, priest and prophet; more than forty identifications have been offered. The point that is clear is that the shepherd removed the bad rulers quickly, within one month.

decisions.choice: impatient with them ... they loathed me: the flock and the shepherd turn against each other
decisions.reason: "Them" most likely means the flock, which the shepherd addresses in the next verse; it may also mean the three shepherds. The relationship between the shepherd and the people breaks down from both sides.

decisions.choice: with the flock (B); of the sheep (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "them" are (m2). Literal keeps "my soul was impatient", "their soul ... loathed", the Hebrew way of saying "I" and "they".

source.text: וָאֹמַ֕ר לֹ֥א אֶרְעֶ֖ה אֶתְכֶ֑ם הַמֵּתָ֣ה תָמ֗וּת וְהַנִּכְחֶ֨דֶת֙ תִּכָּחֵ֔ד וְהַ֨נִּשְׁאָר֔וֹת תֹּאכַ֕לְנָה אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶת־בְּשַׂ֥ר רְעוּתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said, I will not shepherd you; the dying let die, and the being destroyed let be destroyed, and those left let devour each the flesh of her neighbor.

en.L: And I said, "I will not shepherd you. What is dying, let it die; and what is being destroyed, let it be destroyed; and those that are left, let them devour one another's flesh."
en.B: Then I said, "I will not be your shepherd. Let the dying die and the perishing perish, and let those that are left eat one another's flesh."
en.R: Then I said to the sheep, "I will not take care of you any longer. Let the ones that are dying die. Let the ones that are being destroyed be destroyed. Let the ones that are left eat each other's flesh."

es.L: Y dije: «No {{plural_you:los|os}} apacentaré. La que muere, que muera; y la que se pierde, que se pierda; y las que queden, que se coman unas a otras la carne».
es.B: Entonces dije: «No seré {{plural_you:su pastor|vuestro pastor}}. Que muera la que se está muriendo, y que perezca la que está pereciendo, y que las que queden se coman la carne unas a otras».
es.R: Entonces les dije a las ovejas: «Ya no {{plural_you:las|os}} cuidaré más. Que se mueran las que se están muriendo. Que se pierdan las que se están perdiendo. Que las que queden se coman unas a otras».

fr.L: Et je dis : « Je ne vous ferai plus paître. Celle qui meurt, qu’elle meure ; et celle qui périt, qu’elle périsse ; et celles qui restent, qu’elles dévorent la chair l’une de l’autre. »
fr.B: Puis je dis : « Je ne serai plus votre berger. Que celle qui meurt meure, que celle qui périt périsse, et que celles qui restent se dévorent entre elles. »
fr.R: Puis j’ai dit aux moutons : « Je ne m’occuperai plus de vous. Que ceux qui meurent meurent. Que ceux qui sont en train d’être détruits soient détruits. Que ceux qui restent se mangent les uns les autres. »

sw.L: Nikasema, "Sitawachunga. Anayekufa na afe; na anayeangamizwa na aangamizwe; na wale waliobaki na walane nyama kila mmoja ya mwenzake."
sw.B: Kisha nikasema, "Sitakuwa mchungaji wenu. Wanaokufa na wafe, na wanaoangamia na waangamie, na wale waliobaki na walane nyama wao kwa wao."
sw.R: Kisha nikawaambia kondoo, "Sitawatunza tena. Wale wanaokufa na wafe. Wale wanaoangamizwa na waangamizwe. Wale waliobaki na walane nyama wao kwa wao."

vi.L: Rồi tôi nói: "Tôi sẽ không chăn các ngươi nữa. Con nào đang chết, cứ để nó chết; con nào đang bị hủy diệt, cứ để nó bị hủy diệt; còn những con sót lại, cứ để chúng ăn thịt lẫn nhau."
vi.B: Rồi tôi nói: "Tôi sẽ không làm người chăn các ngươi nữa. Con nào sắp chết, cứ để nó chết; con nào sắp bị tiêu diệt, cứ để nó bị tiêu diệt; còn những con sót lại, cứ để chúng ăn thịt lẫn nhau."
vi.R: Rồi tôi nói với đàn chiên: "Tôi sẽ không chăm sóc các ngươi nữa. Con nào sắp chết, cứ để nó chết. Con nào sắp bị tiêu diệt, cứ để nó bị tiêu diệt. Những con còn lại, cứ để chúng ăn thịt lẫn nhau."

ko.L: 그리고 내가 말했다. "나는 너희를 치지 않겠다. 죽을 것은 죽고, 망할 것은 망하고, 남은 것들은 서로 살을 뜯어 먹어라."
ko.B: 그래서 내가 말했다. "나는 더 이상 너희의 목자가 되지 않겠다. 죽어 가는 것은 죽고, 망해 가는 것은 망하고, 남은 것들은 서로 살을 뜯어 먹어라."
ko.R: 그래서 나는 양들에게 말했다. "나는 더 이상 너희를 돌보지 않겠다. 죽어 가는 것들은 죽어라. 망해 가는 것들은 망하여라. 남은 것들은 서로 살을 뜯어 먹어라."

pt.L: E eu disse: "Não apascentarei vocês. A que está morrendo, que morra; e a que está sendo destruída, que seja destruída; e as que restarem, que comam a carne umas das outras."
pt.B: Então eu disse: "Não serei o pastor de vocês. Que morram as que estão morrendo e pereçam as que estão perecendo, e que as que restarem comam a carne umas das outras."
pt.R: Então eu disse às ovelhas: "Não vou mais cuidar de vocês. As que estão morrendo, que morram. As que estão sendo destruídas, que sejam destruídas. As que sobrarem, que comam a carne umas das outras."

decisions.choice: the dying, the being destroyed, those that are left: the sheep are given up to their fate
decisions.reason: The forms are feminine, for the ewes of the flock. The shepherd no longer protects them from death, from destruction or from one another. Ezekiel 34:4 blames the shepherds for leaving the weak to perish; here the shepherd does so as a judgment.

decisions.choice: devour one another's flesh: the people turn on one another
decisions.reason: Sheep do not eat each other; the picture is of a people destroying itself through strife or the horror of famine in a siege (Isaiah 9:19; Jeremiah 19:9).

decisions.choice: said to the sheep; any longer (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the sheep as the ones addressed and breaks the list into short sentences.

decisions.choice: "los" / "las" with plural_you
decisions.reason: The shepherd speaks to the flock in the plural, so the pronoun takes plural_you; R names the sheep, so its pronoun agrees with "ovejas".

decisions.choice: "celle qui meurt ... celles qui restent" (L, B), feminine
decisions.reason: The Hebrew participles are feminine, for the sheep (French "brebis"); Readable says "moutons", masculine.

source.text: וָאֶקַּ֤ח אֶת־מַקְלִי֙ אֶת־נֹ֔עַם וָאֶגְדַּ֖ע אֹת֑וֹ לְהָפֵיר֙ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרַ֖תִּי אֶת־כָּל־הָעַמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I took my staff Favor and cut it in pieces, to break my covenant that I had made with all the peoples.

en.L: And I took my staff Favor and cut it in pieces, to break my covenant that I had made with all the peoples.
en.B: Then I took my staff named Favor and broke it, to annul the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
en.R: Then I took the staff I had named Favor and broke it in pieces. This showed that I was canceling the agreement I had made with all the nations.

es.L: Y tomé mi cayado Favor y lo quebré, para romper mi pacto que había hecho con todos los pueblos.
es.B: Entonces tomé mi cayado llamado Favor y lo quebré, para anular el pacto que había hecho con todos los pueblos.
es.R: Entonces tomé el cayado al que había llamado Favor y lo hice pedazos. Así mostré que anulaba el acuerdo que había hecho con todas las naciones.

fr.L: Et je pris mon bâton Faveur et je le brisai, pour rompre mon alliance que j’avais conclue avec tous les peuples.
fr.B: Je pris alors mon bâton appelé Faveur et je le brisai, pour annuler l’alliance que j’avais conclue avec tous les peuples.
fr.R: Ensuite, j’ai pris le bâton que j’avais appelé Faveur et je l’ai cassé en morceaux. Cela montrait que j’annulais l’accord que j’avais fait avec toutes les nations.

sw.L: Nikaitwaa fimbo yangu Fadhili, nikaikata vipande vipande, ili kulivunja agano langu nililokuwa nimefanya na watu wote wa mataifa.
sw.B: Kisha nikaichukua fimbo yangu iitwayo Fadhili, nikaivunja, ili kulitangua agano nililokuwa nimefanya na watu wote wa mataifa.
sw.R: Kisha nikaichukua ile fimbo niliyokuwa nimeiita Fadhili, nikaivunja vipande vipande. Hii ilionyesha kwamba nilikuwa ninalitangua agano nililokuwa nimefanya na mataifa yote.

vi.L: Tôi lấy cây gậy của tôi là Ân Huệ mà chặt ra từng khúc, để hủy bỏ giao ước của tôi đã lập với mọi dân tộc.
vi.B: Rồi tôi lấy cây gậy tên là Ân Huệ mà bẻ gãy, để hủy bỏ giao ước tôi đã lập với mọi dân tộc.
vi.R: Rồi tôi lấy cây gậy tôi đã đặt tên là Ân Huệ mà bẻ ra từng khúc. Việc này cho thấy tôi đang hủy bỏ giao ước tôi đã lập với mọi dân tộc.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 내 지팡이 '은총'을 가져다가 그것을 꺾어, 내가 모든 백성들과 맺은 내 언약을 깨뜨렸다.
ko.B: 그리고 나는 '은총'이라는 내 지팡이를 가져다가 꺾어 버렸다. 내가 모든 백성들과 맺은 언약을 깨뜨린다는 뜻이었다.
ko.R: 그리고 나는 '은총'이라고 이름 지은 지팡이를 가져다가 부러뜨렸다. 내가 모든 민족과 맺은 약속을 깨뜨린다는 것을 보여 준 것이다.

pt.L: E tomei a minha vara Favor e a quebrei em pedaços, para romper a minha aliança que eu tinha feito com todos os povos.
pt.B: Então peguei a minha vara chamada Favor e a quebrei, para anular a aliança que eu tinha feito com todos os povos.
pt.R: Então peguei o cajado a que eu tinha dado o nome de Favor e o quebrei em pedaços. Isso mostrou que eu estava cancelando o acordo que tinha feito com todas as nações.

decisions.choice: my covenant with all the peoples: the protection that kept the nations back is withdrawn
decisions.reason: The covenant is not explained. It is most likely an agreement that kept the nations from harming the flock, like the covenant with the wild animals in Hosea 2:20 and Ezekiel 34:25. When Favor is broken, that protection ends. The prophet speaks as the shepherd, but the covenant is the LORD's to give and to take away: the people recognize "the word of the LORD" in it (verse 11).

decisions.choice: my staff, my covenant: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The speaker is the prophet acting the part of the shepherd, so his pronouns take no deity_pronoun span, even where he acts for the LORD (m1). Readable says "agreement" for "covenant" and "nations" for "peoples".

decisions.choice: the purpose clause as a second sentence (L, B)
decisions.reason: Korean would put the purpose before the action; a second sentence keeps the Hebrew order of taking, breaking and then the meaning of the act.

decisions.choice: "mon bâton", "mon alliance": no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the English: the prophet speaks while acting out God's part.

decisions.choice: "mi cayado", "mi pacto" without deity_pronoun
decisions.reason: The prophet acts out the LORD's part, but the words are his own, so they take no deity_pronoun span, as in the English.

decisions.choice: the shepherd says "tôi" and "giao ước của tôi", with no deity span
decisions.reason: Zechariah acts the shepherd's part and speaks as himself, as the English has no deity span here.

decisions.choice: "fimbo yangu", "agano langu" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks in the part he acts, as the English, which also has no span here.

source.text: וַתֻּפַ֖ר בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיֵּדְע֨וּ כֵ֜ן עֲנִיֵּ֤י הַצֹּאן֙ הַשֹּׁמְרִ֣ים אֹתִ֔י כִּ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was broken on that day, and so knew the afflicted of the flock who were watching me that [it was the] word of Yahweh.

en.L: And it was broken on that day, and thus the afflicted of the flock, the ones watching me, knew that it [was] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s word.
en.B: It was broken on that day, and the afflicted of the flock who were watching me understood that this was a word from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: So it was canceled that day. The suffering sheep that were watching me knew that this was a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y fue roto en aquel día, y así conocieron los afligidos del rebaño, los que me observaban, que [era] palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Fue anulado aquel día, y los afligidos del rebaño que me observaban comprendieron que era palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Así quedó anulado ese día. Las ovejas que sufrían y que me estaban mirando supieron que aquello era un mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et elle fut rompue en ce jour-là, et ainsi les malheureux du troupeau, ceux qui m’observaient, surent que c’était la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Elle fut rompue ce jour-là, et les malheureux du troupeau qui m’observaient comprirent que c’était une parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Ainsi, l’accord a été annulé ce jour-là. Les moutons qui souffraient et qui me regardaient ont compris que c’était un message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nalo likavunjwa siku ile, na hivyo wanyonge wa kundi, wale walionitazama, wakajua kwamba [hilo lilikuwa] neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Likavunjwa siku ile, na wale wanyonge wa kundi waliokuwa wakinitazama wakatambua kwamba hilo lilikuwa neno kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Basi agano hilo likatanguka siku ile. Kondoo walioteseka, waliokuwa wakinitazama, wakajua kwamba huo ulikuwa ujumbe kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Ngay trong ngày ấy, nó bị hủy bỏ; và như vậy những con khốn khổ trong bầy, là những con đang nhìn tôi, biết rằng ấy [là] lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Ngay ngày ấy giao ước bị hủy bỏ, và những con khốn khổ trong bầy đang theo dõi tôi hiểu rằng đây là lời từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Vậy ngay ngày ấy giao ước bị hủy bỏ. Những con chiên khốn khổ đang theo dõi tôi biết rằng đây là sứ điệp từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: 그날에 그것이 깨어졌다. 그러자 나를 지켜보던 양 떼 가운데 고난받는 것들이 그것이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀인 줄 알았다.
ko.B: 그날 그 언약이 깨어졌다. 나를 지켜보던 양 떼 가운데 고난받는 양들은 이것이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀인 줄 깨달았다.
ko.R: 그날 그 약속은 깨어졌다. 나를 지켜보던 고통받는 양들은 이것이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하신 말씀인 줄 알았다.

pt.L: E ela foi rompida naquele dia, e assim os aflitos do rebanho, os que me observavam, souberam que [era] a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: Ela foi rompida naquele dia, e os aflitos do rebanho, que me observavam, entenderam que aquilo era uma palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.R: Assim o acordo foi cancelado naquele dia. As ovelhas sofredoras que estavam me observando entenderam que aquilo era uma mensagem {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.

decisions.choice: the afflicted of the flock: following the Hebrew text, as in verse 7
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, the Septuagint reads "the Canaanites", that is, the sheep traders, in place of "so the afflicted". Read that way, it is the traders who were watching and understood. The Hebrew text is kept here.

decisions.choice: who were watching me ... knew that it was the word of the LORD: the faithful few understood
decisions.reason: The poor of the flock watched what the shepherd did and saw in it a message from the LORD. A word from the LORD is shown to be true when it comes to pass (Deuteronomy 18:22; Jeremiah 32:8).

decisions.choice: on that day (every level)
decisions.reason: Here "on that day" refers to a day in the past, in the story, not to the coming day of the LORD, so it is not the prophetic formula of the Isaiah table, and every level says "on that day" (Readable "that day").

decisions.choice: "en aquel día" (L); "aquel día" (B); "ese día" (R)
decisions.reason: Here the phrase dates an event in the story, so R says "ese día", the term sheet's second R form.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם אִם־ט֧וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֛ם הָב֥וּ שְׂכָרִ֖י וְאִם־לֹ֣א׀חֲדָ֑לוּ וַיִּשְׁקְל֥וּ אֶת־שְׂכָרִ֖י שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים כָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said to them, If [it is] good in your eyes, give my wages; and if not, refrain. And they weighed out my wages, thirty [of] silver.

en.L: And I said to them, "If [it is] good in your eyes, give [me] my wages; and if not, keep [them]." And they weighed out my wages, thirty [pieces of] silver.
en.B: Then I said to them, "If you think it right, give me my pay; but if not, keep it." So they weighed out my pay: thirty pieces of silver.
en.R: Then I said to them, "If you think it is right, pay me my wages. But if not, keep your money." So they weighed out thirty pieces of silver to pay me.

es.L: Y les dije: «Si [es] bueno a {{plural_you:sus ojos|vuestros ojos}}, {{plural_you:denme|dadme}} mi salario; y si no, {{plural_you:déjenlo|dejadlo}}». Y pesaron mi salario, treinta [piezas de] plata.
es.B: Entonces les dije: «Si {{plural_you:les|os}} parece bien, {{plural_you:denme|dadme}} mi paga; y si no, {{plural_you:guárdensela|guardáosla}}». Así que me pesaron como paga treinta monedas de plata.
es.R: Entonces les dije: «Si {{plural_you:les|os}} parece justo, {{plural_you:páguenme|pagadme}} mi salario. Si no, {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} con {{plural_you:su dinero|vuestro dinero}}». Así que pesaron treinta monedas de plata para pagarme.

fr.L: Et je leur dis : « Si [c’est] bon à vos yeux, donnez[-moi] mon salaire ; et sinon, gardez[-le]. » Et ils pesèrent mon salaire : trente [pièces] d’argent.
fr.B: Je leur dis alors : « Si cela vous semble juste, donnez-moi ma paie ; sinon, gardez-la. » Ils pesèrent ma paie : trente pièces d’argent.
fr.R: Puis je leur ai dit : « Si vous trouvez que c’est juste, payez-moi mon salaire. Sinon, gardez votre argent. » Alors ils ont pesé trente pièces d’argent pour me payer.

sw.L: Nikawaambia, "Ikiwa [ni] vema machoni penu, nipeni mshahara wangu; na kama sivyo, acheni." Nao wakanipimia mshahara wangu, thelathini [vipande vya] fedha.
sw.B: Kisha nikawaambia, "Kama mnaona ni haki, nipeni ujira wangu; lakini kama sivyo, ubakini nao." Basi wakanipimia ujira wangu: vipande thelathini vya fedha.
sw.R: Kisha nikawaambia, "Kama mnaona ni haki, nilipeni mshahara wangu. Lakini kama sivyo, bakini na pesa zenu." Basi wakanipimia vipande thelathini vya fedha kunilipa.

vi.L: Tôi nói với họ: "Nếu các ông thấy là tốt, hãy trả tiền công cho tôi; còn nếu không, thì thôi." Vậy họ cân tiền công cho tôi, ba mươi [miếng] bạc.
vi.B: Rồi tôi nói với họ: "Nếu các ông thấy là phải, hãy trả công cho tôi; còn nếu không, thì cứ giữ lấy." Vậy họ cân tiền công cho tôi: ba mươi đồng bạc.
vi.R: Rồi tôi nói với họ: "Nếu các ông thấy là đúng, hãy trả tiền công cho tôi. Còn nếu không, thì cứ giữ tiền lại." Vậy họ cân ba mươi đồng bạc để trả công cho tôi.

ko.L: 내가 그들에게 말했다. "여러분의 눈에 좋으면 내 품삯을 주시오. 그렇지 않으면 그만두시오." 그러자 그들이 내 품삯으로 은 서른 [닢을] 달아 주었다.
ko.B: 내가 그들에게 말했다. "여러분이 옳다고 여기면 내 품삯을 주시오. 그렇지 않으면 그만두시오." 그러자 그들이 내 품삯으로 은돈 서른 닢을 달아 주었다.
ko.R: 내가 그들에게 말했다. "여러분이 옳다고 생각하면 내 품삯을 주시오. 그렇지 않으면 주지 마시오." 그러자 그들은 은돈 서른 닢을 달아서 나에게 주었다.

pt.L: E eu lhes disse: "Se [é] bom aos olhos de vocês, deem[-me] o meu salário; e, se não, fiquem [com ele]." E pesaram o meu salário, trinta [moedas de] prata.
pt.B: Então eu lhes disse: "Se acham justo, deem-me o meu pagamento; mas, se não, fiquem com ele." Então pesaram o meu pagamento: trinta moedas de prata.
pt.R: Então eu disse a eles: "Se vocês acham que é justo, paguem o meu salário. Mas, se não acham, fiquem com o seu dinheiro." Então eles pesaram trinta moedas de prata para me pagar.

decisions.choice: they weighed out thirty pieces of silver: the price of a slave
decisions.reason: Silver was weighed, not counted, before coins were common; the unit is the shekel, about two-fifths of an ounce. Thirty shekels was the payment the law set for a slave gored by an ox (Exodus 21:32). The wage was an insult: it valued the shepherd's work, and so the LORD's care for his people, at the price of a slave.

decisions.choice: to them: those who hired the shepherd
decisions.reason: The text does not say who "they" are: the sheep traders, the owners of the flock, or the leaders of the people. They are those for whom the shepherd worked and who now pay him off.

decisions.choice: thirty pieces of silver: Matthew 26:15 and 27:9
decisions.reason: In Matthew 26:15 the chief priests pay Judas thirty pieces of silver to betray Jesus, and Matthew 27:3-10 sees this passage fulfilled when the money is thrown into the temple and used to buy the potter's field (see verse 13).

decisions.choice: thirty [pieces of] silver (L); thirty pieces of silver (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "thirty silver"; every level names pieces of silver, as the reader knows them from Matthew, and Literal brackets the supplied words.

decisions.choice: "treinta [piezas de] plata" (L); "treinta monedas de plata" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording matches Matthew 26:15 and 27:9 in Spanish at each level, so the allusion can be seen.

decisions.choice: "trente [pièces] d'argent" (L), "trente pièces d'argent" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the published Matthew 26:15 and 27:9, which take up this verse, as the term sheet asks.

decisions.choice: "thelathini [vipande vya] fedha" (L); "vipande thelathini vya fedha" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The published Swahili of Matthew 26:15 and 27:9 says "vipande thelathini vya fedha"; Balanced and Readable use the same words so the reader can see the link.

decisions.choice: "ba mươi [miếng] bạc" (L) / "ba mươi đồng bạc" (B, R), as Matthew 26:15 and 27:9; Zechariah says "các ông" to those who hired him
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording, shared with the Gospel so the reader can see the quotation; L brackets the unit the Hebrew leaves out.

decisions.choice: "은 서른 [닢]" (L); "은돈 서른 닢" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and the Korean Matthew 27:9, so the quotation is visible.

decisions.choice: The shepherd speaks to his employers in 하오체 with "여러분"
decisions.reason: As Ezekiel speaks to the people in his own voice (term sheet section 3): neither the 합쇼체 of a servant nor the 해라체 God uses.

decisions.choice: trinta [moedas de] prata (L); trinta moedas de prata (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wage (m1) is named in the words Matthew 26:15 and 27:9 have in Portuguese, "as trinta moedas de prata" (m3), as the English does (r-en-1); Literal brackets the supplied words. The pieces are not converted, since the number thirty is the point.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י הַשְׁלִיכֵ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר אֶ֣דֶר הַיְקָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָקַ֖רְתִּי מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וָֽאֶקְחָה֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים הַכֶּ֔סֶף וָאַשְׁלִ֥יךְ אֹת֛וֹ בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־הַיּוֹצֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh said to me, Throw it to the potter, the magnificence of the price at which I was priced by them. And I took the thirty [of] silver and threw it [into the] house of Yahweh, to the potter.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Throw it to the potter, the magnificent price at which I was priced by them!" So I took the thirty [pieces of] silver and threw it [in] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the potter.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Throw it to the potter, that fine price they set on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}!" Taking the thirty pieces of silver, I threw them into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the potter.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Throw the money to the potter. That is how little they think I am worth!" So I took the thirty pieces of silver to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and threw them to the potter.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «¡Échalo al alfarero, el magnífico precio en que fui valorado por ellos!». Y tomé las treinta [piezas de] plata y las eché [en] la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, al alfarero.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «¡Échaselo al alfarero, ese buen precio en que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} valoraron!». Tomé las treinta monedas de plata y las eché en la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, al alfarero.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Échale el dinero al alfarero. ¡Eso es lo poco que creen que valgo!». Así que llevé las treinta monedas de plata al templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y se las eché al alfarero.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Jette-le au potier, ce prix magnifique auquel ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont estimé ! » Et je pris les trente [pièces] d’argent et je les jetai [dans] la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, au potier.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Jette-le au potier, ce beau prix auquel ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont estimé ! » Je pris les trente pièces d’argent et les jetai dans la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, au potier.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a dit : « Jette l’argent au potier. Voilà le peu de valeur qu’ils pensent que j’ai ! » Alors j’ai pris les trente pièces d’argent, je suis allé au temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et je les ai jetées au potier.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Mtupie mfinyanzi, ile thamani tukufu niliyothaminiwa nao!" Basi nikavichukua vile thelathini [vipande vya] fedha, nikavitupa [ndani ya] nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa mfinyanzi.
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Mtupie mfinyanzi, hiyo bei nzuri walionikadiria!" Nikavichukua vile vipande thelathini vya fedha, nikavitupa ndani ya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa mfinyanzi.
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Mtupie mfinyanzi pesa hizo. Ndivyo walivyoona kwamba sina thamani kubwa!" Basi nikavichukua vile vipande thelathini vya fedha mpaka hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nikamtupia mfinyanzi.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Hãy ném nó cho thợ gốm, cái giá cao quý mà chúng đã định cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}!" Vậy tôi lấy ba mươi [miếng] bạc và ném vào nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, cho thợ gốm.
vi.B: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Hãy ném số bạc ấy cho thợ gốm, cái giá hậu hĩnh mà chúng đã định cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}!" Tôi lấy ba mươi đồng bạc và ném vào nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, cho thợ gốm.
vi.R: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Hãy ném số tiền ấy cho thợ gốm. Chúng coi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} rẻ mạt đến thế đấy!" Vậy tôi mang ba mươi đồng bạc đến đền thờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và ném cho thợ gốm.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "그것을 토기장이에게 던져라. 그들이 나를 값 매긴 그 훌륭한 값을!" 그래서 내가 은 서른 [닢을] 가져다가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에서 토기장이에게 던졌다.
ko.B: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "그것을 토기장이에게 던져 버려라. 그들이 나에게 매긴 그 대단한 값을!" 그래서 나는 은돈 서른 닢을 가져다가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에 있는 토기장이에게 던졌다.
ko.R: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "그 돈을 그릇 만드는 사람에게 던져 버려라. 그들은 나를 그 정도 값어치밖에 안 된다고 여겼다!" 그래서 나는 은돈 서른 닢을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전으로 가져가서 그릇 만드는 사람에게 던졌다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Lança-o ao oleiro, esse magnífico preço em que fui avaliado por eles!" Então tomei as trinta [moedas de] prata e as lancei [na] casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, ao oleiro.
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Lança-o ao oleiro, esse belo preço em que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} avaliaram!" Peguei as trinta moedas de prata e as lancei na casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, ao oleiro.

decisions.choice: the magnificent price at which I was priced by them: said in scorn
decisions.reason: The LORD calls the thirty shekels a "magnificent price", in bitter irony. In the shepherd's wage the people had set a value on the LORD himself, and it was the price of a slave (verse 12). Here the LORD speaks of himself as the one priced.

decisions.choice: the potter: following the Hebrew text
alternatives: to the treasury (a change of one letter, as the Syriac reads)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "to the potter", both times. A potter may have worked for the temple, making vessels for its use, and throwing the money to him showed contempt for it, as something to be thrown away to a maker of cheap pots. The Syriac reads "to the treasury", which differs by one letter in Hebrew, and many readers follow it: the money was thrown into the temple treasury. The Hebrew text is kept here.

decisions.choice: quoted in Matthew 27:9-10, which names Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Matthew 27:9-10 sees this verse fulfilled when the chief priests take the thirty pieces of silver Judas threw into the temple and buy the potter's field. Matthew names the prophet Jeremiah. The words are closest to these verses, but Matthew joins them with themes from Jeremiah: the potter's house (Jeremiah 18:1-12), the potter's jar broken at the valley of slaughter (Jeremiah 19), and the field bought with silver (Jeremiah 32:6-15). The usual explanation is that he names the better-known prophet whose words also shape the quotation; some add that the scroll of the prophets was sometimes called by the name of Jeremiah, which stood first in it.

decisions.choice: the magnificent price at which I was priced (L); that fine price they set on me (B); how little they think I am worth (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the irony of the Hebrew (m1); Readable says plainly what it means. The LORD speaks of himself, so "me" takes the deity_pronoun setting at Balanced. Readable says "temple" for "the house of the LORD".

decisions.choice: "al alfarero"
decisions.reason: The potter is kept at every level, as the Hebrew has it and as Matthew 27:10 in Spanish has "el campo del alfarero".

decisions.choice: "le potier" at every level
decisions.reason: As the Hebrew text and the published Matthew 27:9-10; the other reading is in the English footnote.

decisions.choice: "mfinyanzi" (the potter) at every level
decisions.reason: Following the Hebrew text, as the English; the published Matthew 27:10 also has "shamba la mfinyanzi". The meaning decision's footnote gives the reading "treasury".

decisions.choice: "thợ gốm", as Matthew 27:9-10
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording, so the allusion in Matthew is visible; the other reading (treasury) is in the English footnote.

decisions.choice: "토기장이" (L, B); "그릇 만드는 사람" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and Jeremiah; Matthew 27:9-10 quotes this verse under Jeremiah's name, and the Korean Matthew also has "토기장이".

decisions.choice: "el magnífico precio"
decisions.reason: The scorn of "magnificent" is kept at L; B says "ese buen precio" with the same irony, and R says it plainly.

decisions.choice: Lança-o ao oleiro (L, B); o preço em que fui avaliado (L); avaliar; o oleiro
decisions.reason: Matthew 27:9-10 quotes these words (m3), so Portuguese keeps their wording where the Hebrew is the same: "as trinta moedas de prata", "avaliado", "o oleiro". Here Matthew follows its own form of the text and the Hebrew differs: the Hebrew has the LORD say "fui avaliado" of himself (m1) and the money thrown "ao oleiro" in the house of the LORD (m2), so Portuguese follows the Hebrew and does not add Matthew's "campo". "Me" for the LORD takes the setting at Balanced, as in the English.

pt.B: Então quebrei a minha segunda vara, União, para romper os laços de irmandade entre Judá e Israel.

decisions.choice: to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel: the people's unity undone
decisions.reason: The staff named Union stood for the bonds that held the people together. Breaking it undoes the hope of a reunited people, which Ezekiel 37:15-22 pictured with two sticks joined into one in the prophet's hand, and which Zechariah 9:13 and 10:6 promised. The text does not say how the break came about.

decisions.choice: the one I had named Union; This showed that ... the family ties (R)
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader of the staff's name and says what breaking it meant, as in verse 10.

ko.B: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "다시 한 번 어리석은 목자의 도구들을 챙겨라.

pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Toma mais uma vez o equipamento de um pastor insensato.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Pega de novo as coisas que um pastor usa, mas desta vez age como um pastor sem juízo.

decisions.choice: the equipment of a shepherd: his staff, his bag and his sling
decisions.reason: A shepherd carried a staff, a bag for food and a sling for driving off wild animals (1 Samuel 17:40). The prophet is to take them up again and act out a second part.

decisions.choice: foolish: morally foolish, careless of what is right
decisions.reason: In the Bible a fool is not simply stupid, but someone who despises wisdom and does as he pleases (Proverbs 1:7). Verse 16 shows what such a shepherd does, and verse 17 calls him worthless.

decisions.choice: but this time act like a shepherd who is a fool (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the prophet is to do with the equipment: act the part of a foolish shepherd.

decisions.choice: "los aperos de un pastor insensato" (L, B); "un pastor necio" (R)
decisions.reason: The shepherd's gear (staff, bag, sling) is "aperos"; "insensato" is the moral fool of Proverbs.

records.literal_gloss: For look, I [am] raising up a shepherd in the land; the perishing he will not visit, the young he will not seek, and the broken he will not heal, the standing he will not sustain; and [the] flesh of the fat he will eat, and their hooves he will tear off.

en.L: For look, I am raising up a shepherd in the land; the perishing he will not care for, the young he will not seek, and the broken he will not heal, the healthy he will not sustain; but the flesh of the fat he will eat, and their hooves he will tear off."
en.B: For I am about to raise up a shepherd in the land who will not care for the perishing, or look for the young, or heal the injured, or feed the healthy, but will eat the meat of the fat sheep and tear off their hooves."
en.R: I am going to give the land a shepherd who will not care about the sheep that are dying. He will not look for the young ones or heal the ones that are hurt. He will not feed the healthy ones. Instead, he will eat the meat of the fat sheep and even tear off their hooves."

es.L: Porque he aquí, yo levanto un pastor en la tierra; no cuidará de la que perece, no buscará a la pequeña, no curará a la quebrada, no sustentará a la sana; sino que comerá la carne de la gorda y le arrancará las pezuñas».
es.B: Porque voy a levantar en la tierra un pastor que no cuidará de las que perecen, ni buscará a las pequeñas, ni curará a las heridas, ni alimentará a las sanas, sino que se comerá la carne de las gordas y les arrancará las pezuñas».
es.R: Voy a darle a la tierra un pastor que no se preocupará por las ovejas que se mueren. No buscará a las pequeñas ni curará a las que están heridas. No alimentará a las sanas. En cambio, se comerá la carne de las ovejas gordas y hasta les arrancará las pezuñas».

fr.L: Car voici, je suscite un berger dans le pays ; celles qui périssent, il ne s’en souciera pas ; les jeunes, il ne les cherchera pas ; et celle qui est blessée, il ne la guérira pas ; celle qui se tient debout, il ne la nourrira pas ; mais la chair des grasses, il la mangera, et leurs sabots, il les arrachera. »
fr.B: Car je vais susciter dans le pays un berger qui ne se souciera pas des brebis qui périssent, ne cherchera pas les jeunes, ne soignera pas les blessées, ne nourrira pas celles qui sont en bonne santé, mais mangera la viande des plus grasses et leur arrachera les sabots. »
fr.R: Je vais donner au pays un berger qui ne s’occupera pas des moutons en train de mourir. Il ne cherchera pas les jeunes et il ne soignera pas ceux qui sont blessés. Il ne nourrira pas ceux qui sont en bonne santé. Au contraire, il mangera la viande des moutons gras et il leur arrachera même les sabots. »

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, ninainua mchungaji katika nchi; wanaoangamia hatawajali, walio wachanga hatawatafuta, na waliovunjika hatawaponya, walio wazima hatawalisha; bali nyama ya walionona ataila, na kwato zao atazirarua."
sw.B: Kwa maana karibu nitainua mchungaji katika nchi ambaye hatawajali wanaoangamia, wala hatawatafuta walio wachanga, wala hatawaponya waliojeruhiwa, wala hatawalisha walio wazima, bali atakula nyama ya kondoo walionona na kurarua kwato zao."
sw.R: Nitaipa nchi mchungaji ambaye hatajali kondoo wanaokufa. Hatawatafuta wale wachanga wala kuwaponya wale walioumia. Hatawalisha wale walio wazima. Badala yake, atakula nyama ya kondoo walionona na hata kurarua kwato zao."

vi.L: Vì kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ dấy lên một người chăn trong xứ; con đang chết nó sẽ không chăm sóc, con non nó sẽ không tìm kiếm, con bị gãy nó sẽ không chữa lành, con còn khỏe nó sẽ không nuôi dưỡng; nhưng thịt của con béo nó sẽ ăn, và móng của chúng nó sẽ xé ra."
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp dấy lên trong xứ một người chăn không chăm sóc con sắp chết, không tìm kiếm con non, không chữa lành con bị thương, không nuôi dưỡng con khỏe mạnh, nhưng lại ăn thịt những con béo và xé cả móng chúng ra."
vi.R: Ta sẽ ban cho xứ này một người chăn không lo gì đến những con chiên sắp chết. Nó sẽ không tìm kiếm những con non hay chữa lành những con bị thương. Nó sẽ không cho những con khỏe mạnh ăn. Thay vào đó, nó sẽ ăn thịt những con chiên béo và còn xé cả móng chúng ra."

ko.L: 보라, 내가 이 땅에 한 목자를 일으키겠다. 그는 망해 가는 것을 돌보지 않고, 어린 것을 찾지 않으며, 다친 것을 고치지 않고, 성한 것을 먹이지 않을 것이다. 오히려 살진 것들의 고기를 먹고, 그것들의 발굽까지 찢을 것이다."
ko.B: 보아라, 내가 이 땅에 한 목자를 세우겠다. 그는 죽어 가는 양을 돌보지 않고, 어린 양을 찾지 않으며, 다친 양을 고치지 않고, 튼튼한 양을 먹이지 않을 것이다. 오히려 살진 양의 고기를 먹고, 그 발굽까지 뜯어낼 것이다."
ko.R: 나는 이 땅에 한 목자를 세우겠다. 그는 죽어 가는 양들을 돌보지 않을 것이다. 어린 양들을 찾지 않고, 다친 양들을 고쳐 주지 않을 것이다. 튼튼한 양들도 먹이지 않을 것이다. 오히려 살진 양들의 고기를 먹고, 발굽까지 뜯어낼 것이다."

pt.L: Porque eis que levanto um pastor na terra; da que perece ele não cuidará, a jovem ele não buscará, e a ferida ele não curará, a sadia ele não sustentará; mas a carne da gorda ele comerá, e os cascos delas arrancará."
pt.B: Porque vou levantar na terra um pastor que não cuidará das que estão perecendo, nem procurará as novas, nem curará as feridas, nem alimentará as sadias, mas comerá a carne das ovelhas gordas e arrancará os seus cascos."
pt.R: Vou dar à terra um pastor que não vai cuidar das ovelhas que estão morrendo. Ele não vai procurar as novas nem curar as que estão feridas. Não vai alimentar as que têm saúde. Em vez disso, vai comer a carne das ovelhas gordas e até arrancar os cascos delas."

decisions.choice: a shepherd who will not care for the perishing: the bad shepherds of Ezekiel 34
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 34:2-4 charges the shepherds of Israel with the same failures: they did not strengthen the weak, heal the sick, bind up the injured or seek the lost, but ate the fat and clothed themselves with the wool. This shepherd is the LORD's judgment on a flock that rejected the good shepherd (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the young: the young of the flock
decisions.reason: The word usually means a youth. Some read it as "the scattered" or "the straying", from a similar word, which would fit Ezekiel 34:4, "the lost you have not sought". The sense of the list is the same: the shepherd neglects every sheep that needs him.

decisions.choice: eat the meat of the fat and tear off their hooves: greed that leaves nothing
decisions.reason: The shepherd eats the best of the flock, and even tears the hooves apart for the last scraps of meat, or by driving the sheep without care. He lives off the flock instead of caring for it.

decisions.choice: who will not care for ... (B); He will not ... (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts each sheep first, for emphasis: "the perishing he will not care for". Literal keeps that order; Balanced and Readable use the order English expects. The LORD's words end here.

decisions.choice: the bad shepherd is "nó" (L, R)
decisions.reason: Contempt for the worthless shepherd, as the oracles speak of the guilty.

records.literal_gloss: Woe [to] the shepherd of worthlessness, abandoning the flock! A sword [be] on his arm and on his right eye! His arm will wither completely, and his right eye will grow completely dim.

en.L: Woe, worthless shepherd, who abandons the flock! \q A sword on his arm and on his right eye! \q His arm will wither completely, \q and his right eye will grow completely dim.
en.B: Woe to the worthless shepherd who deserts the flock! \q May the sword strike his arm and his right eye! \q Let his arm wither away, \q and his right eye go completely blind!
en.R: How terrible it will be for the worthless shepherd who deserts the sheep! \q A sword will strike his arm and his right eye. \q His arm will become completely useless, \q and his right eye will become totally blind.

es.L: ¡Ay del pastor inútil que abandona el rebaño! \q ¡Espada sobre su brazo y sobre su ojo derecho! \q Su brazo se secará por completo, \q y su ojo derecho quedará del todo oscurecido.
es.B: ¡Ay del pastor inútil que abandona el rebaño! \q ¡Que la espada le hiera el brazo y el ojo derecho! \q ¡Que se le seque el brazo del todo, \q y que su ojo derecho quede completamente ciego!
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para el pastor inútil que abandona a las ovejas! \q Una espada le herirá el brazo y el ojo derecho. \q Su brazo quedará completamente inútil, \q y su ojo derecho quedará totalmente ciego.

fr.L: Malheur, berger de néant, qui abandonne le troupeau ! \q L’épée sur son bras et sur son œil droit ! \q Son bras se desséchera complètement, \q et son œil droit s’éteindra complètement.
fr.B: Malheur au berger de rien qui abandonne le troupeau ! \q Que l’épée frappe son bras et son œil droit ! \q Que son bras se dessèche entièrement, \q et que son œil droit devienne tout à fait aveugle !
fr.R: Quel malheur pour le berger qui ne vaut rien et qui abandonne les moutons ! \q Une épée frappera son bras et son œil droit. \q Son bras ne pourra plus servir à rien, \q et son œil droit deviendra complètement aveugle.

sw.L: Ole, mchungaji asiyefaa kitu, anayeliacha kundi! \q Upanga juu ya mkono wake na juu ya jicho lake la kuume! \q Mkono wake utanyauka kabisa, \q na jicho lake la kuume litafifia kabisa.
sw.B: Ole wake mchungaji asiyefaa kitu, anayeliacha kundi! \q Upanga na upige mkono wake na jicho lake la kuume! \q Mkono wake na unyauke kabisa, \q na jicho lake la kuume lipofuke kabisa!
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya sana kwa mchungaji asiyefaa kitu, anayewaacha kondoo! \q Upanga utapiga mkono wake na jicho lake la kuume. \q Mkono wake hautafaa kitu tena, \q na jicho lake la kuume litapofuka kabisa.

vi.L: Khốn cho người chăn vô dụng, kẻ bỏ bầy chiên! \q Gươm [giáng] trên cánh tay nó và trên mắt phải nó! \q Cánh tay nó sẽ khô héo hoàn toàn, \q và mắt phải nó sẽ mù hẳn.
vi.B: Khốn cho người chăn vô dụng, kẻ bỏ mặc bầy chiên! \q Nguyện gươm đánh vào cánh tay và mắt phải nó! \q Nguyện cánh tay nó teo héo, \q và mắt phải nó mù lòa hoàn toàn!
vi.R: Thật khốn khổ cho người chăn vô dụng, kẻ bỏ mặc đàn chiên! \q Gươm sẽ đánh vào cánh tay và mắt phải của nó. \q Cánh tay nó sẽ hoàn toàn vô dụng, \q và mắt phải nó sẽ mù hẳn.

ko.L: 양 떼를 버리는 쓸모없는 목자에게 화가 있다! \q 칼이 그의 팔과 그의 오른쪽 눈 위에 [내릴 것이다]! \q 그의 팔은 아주 말라 버리고, \q 그의 오른쪽 눈은 아주 어두워질 것이다.
ko.B: 양 떼를 버리는 쓸모없는 목자에게 화가 있다! \q 칼이 그의 팔과 오른쪽 눈을 치기를! \q 그의 팔은 바싹 말라 버리고, \q 그의 오른쪽 눈은 아주 멀어 버리기를!
ko.R: 양들을 버리는 쓸모없는 목자에게 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다! \q 칼이 그의 팔과 오른쪽 눈을 칠 것이다. \q 그의 팔은 아주 쓸모없게 되고, \q 그의 오른쪽 눈은 완전히 멀어 버릴 것이다.

pt.L: Ai, pastor inútil, que abandona o rebanho! \q Espada sobre o seu braço e sobre o seu olho direito! \q O seu braço secará por completo, \q e o seu olho direito ficará totalmente escurecido.
pt.B: Ai do pastor inútil que abandona o rebanho! \q Que a espada fira o seu braço e o seu olho direito! \q Que o seu braço fique seco \q e o seu olho direito fique totalmente cego!
pt.R: Que desgraça vai cair sobre o pastor que não vale nada e abandona as ovelhas! \q Uma espada vai ferir o braço dele e o seu olho direito. \q O braço dele vai ficar totalmente inútil, \q e o seu olho direito vai ficar completamente cego.

decisions.choice: the worthless shepherd: a shepherd of no worth, like an idol
decisions.reason: The word for "worthless" means "nothingness", and it is a common word for idols, the "worthless gods" (Leviticus 19:4; Isaiah 2:8). The shepherd who abandons the flock is as useless as an idol.

decisions.choice: a sword on his arm and on his right eye: judgment on his strength and his sight
decisions.reason: The arm is a shepherd's strength to protect the flock, and the eye his watchfulness. He used neither for the sheep, and he will lose both. The right side was the stronger and more valued side.

decisions.choice: woe ... the sword ... will wither: a curse that is also a prediction
alternatives: a sword will strike his arm (as a statement)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb in the line about the sword, which may be read as a wish ("may the sword strike") or as a statement ("the sword will strike"). The last lines are statements about what will happen. The poem returns to the shepherd in 13:7-9, where the LORD calls for the sword against his shepherd.

decisions.choice: Woe (L); Woe to (B); How terrible it will be for (R)
decisions.reason: The cry *hoy* follows the wording set in Isaiah. Balanced reads the sword line as a wish, Readable as a statement; Literal keeps the Hebrew without a verb (m3).
